header_chirho: For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. - John 3:16
primary_goal_chirho: Turn Lineluya into a sensibly designed Rust kernel by hardening core primitives, deleting workaround glue, and making real Alpine workloads validate the kernel without shaping generic semantics.

project_state_summary_chirho.current_milestone_chirho: 15 Alpine SSH commands verified, including real .ko loading via SSH, and 6-7 consecutive SSH sessions per QEMU instance
verified_runtime_chirho: 15 SSH commands verified over the live Alpine/dropbear path, including uname -a, id, date, ls /, cat /proc/meminfo, cat /proc/version, sqlite3 DB ops, python3 -c 'print(42)', and insmod of a real Alpine-built .ko file
6-7 consecutive SSH sessions per QEMU instance now succeed; the old second-connection frontier is no longer the main kernel story
Dropbear boots from ext4 rootfs and reaches real auth, session, fork, exec, pipe, zombie reaping, and TCP paths under repeated workload pressure
Per-process page tables, COW, dynamic musl ELF loading, signals, VFS, PTY, TCP, blocking pipe reads, a 512-entry ext4 cache, and the kernel module loader are all live and under pressure
The GLOBAL_MAPPER corruption frontier materially receded; the current kernel-shaped limiter is fd-table and childpipe lifecycle cleanup, not basic exec viability
project_state_summary_chirho.current_blocker_chirho: The main kernel-shaped blocker is childpipe lifecycle and pipe endpoint cleanup across exec/fd-table cloning: consecutive SSH sessions still cap around 7 because the parent select/read path does not yet observe childpipe write-end closure through one authoritative fd/OFD/pipe lifetime model. Secondary limits are python3 cold-start I/O and remaining demo items (loop mount and module load over SSH).
project_state_summary_chirho.interpretation_chirho: The address-space frontier improved enough that the next phase should center on authoritative fd-table/OFD/pipe lifetime semantics and teardown deletion, while treating performance and remaining demo items as secondary unless they expose a generic primitive gap.

non_negotiable_direction_chirho: No new workload-specific behavior in generic syscall, scheduler, close, exit, select, poll, read, write, or networking primitives.
No protocol-specific shortcuts in VFS, sockets, PTY, signal handling, or process teardown.
Every workaround must name the real primitive that replaces it and the deletion condition for removing the workaround.
Workloads validate primitives; workloads do not define generic semantics.
The architecture should converge toward typed invariants, smaller unsafe boundaries, and fewer global state coordination sites.

architecture_principles_chirho: One authoritative arch-transition boundary should own current-task installation, kernel stack selection, CR3 switching, FS/GS restore, signal entry/return, and return-to-user framing.
Every blocking syscall must either sleep on a waitqueue, wake because the condition became true, or return -EINTR for a deliverable signal.
Exec must authoritatively replace the old user address space; shared boot-PML4 execution must shrink to bounded bootstrap-only behavior.
Fd dispatch should be based on typed open-file-description identity, not inode-mode inference.
Teardown semantics must be explicit for pipes, sockets, PTYs, SIGCHLD, wait4, and session lifecycle.
Unsafe code should live in a smaller substrate with crisp interfaces to higher-level kernel services.
system_invariants_chirho: A task cannot be runnable and blocked at the same time.
A blocked task is blocked for exactly one explicit reason.
A task in Sleeping state is on exactly one waitqueue.
Only the arch-transition layer may mutate CR3, kernel stack top, FS/GS, or user return frames.
Every user task has one authoritative address-space owner.
User-memory mutation routes through checked address-space-aware helpers.
Every fd resolves to one stable typed file description.
Fd-table entry lifetime and open-file-description lifetime are separate.
Signal delivery is an explicit state transition, not an implicit side effect.
Child exit status publication precedes parent wake and reaping visibility.
Pipe and socket readiness fall out of endpoint state, not workload-specific branches.

workstreams_chirho.title_chirho: Authoritative Blocking, Wake, and Signal Interruption
workstreams_chirho.why_now_chirho: This is the biggest cross-cutting weakness and it directly affects SSH teardown, daemons, sockets, pipes, wait4, select, and poll.
success_criteria_chirho: Every core blocking path uses waitqueue sleep or returns -EINTR.
No generic blocking path relies on yield loops or bounded HLT loops in steady state.
Signal interruption behavior is consistent across select, poll, wait4, socket read, pipe read, and accept.
tasks_for_codex_chirho: Own the architecture of the unified blocking contract.
Define the exact interruption rules and restart policy boundaries.
Audit which blocking APIs are still hybrid and decide migration order.
Design the deletion plan for yield-loop and spin-retry fallbacks.
tasks_for_claude_chirho: Implement waitqueue conversions and runtime tests after Codex decomposition.
Instrument and verify wake ordering and EINTR behavior.
Remove transitional loops once authoritative wait paths are live.
tasks_for_gemini_chirho: Audit the planned blocking model against Linux and Asterinas patterns.
Review whether the chosen interruption contract is coherent and minimal.
deletion_targets_chirho: ad hoc signal wake logic not tied to deliverable-signal checks

workstreams_chirho.why_now_chirho: Current-task, kernel stack, CR3, FS/GS, and return-to-user sequencing have already caused repeated correctness failures.
success_criteria_chirho: One explicit switch-to boundary owns context activation and user return setup.
No idle-wake, resume, or scheduler side branch partially reproduces switch logic.
FS/GS, CR3, kernel stack top, TSS.RSP0, and current-task state are restored exactly once per transition.
tasks_for_codex_chirho: Design the switch_to_chirho boundary and its invariants.
Define what low-level state belongs in the substrate versus the scheduler policy layer.
Audit all current state-mutation sites and produce the consolidation map.
tasks_for_claude_chirho: Refactor switch paths toward the single boundary.
Move duplicated state sync code behind the new boundary.
Run trace validation for user return, signal return, idle wake, and syscall return.
tasks_for_gemini_chirho: Audit the boundary design against Asterinas substrate ideas and Rust-safe transition modeling.
deletion_targets_chirho: partial state sync branches in scheduler paths
duplicated CR3 or FS/GS restore logic
global mutation sites outside the switch boundary

workstreams_chirho.why_now_chirho: The worst exec corruption frontier was materially reduced, but hybrid cleanup and bootstrap-only fallback paths are still debt that must not creep back in while the current fd/pipe lifecycle frontier is being resolved.
success_criteria_chirho: Exec replaces the old user mappings authoritatively.
Boot-PML4 user execution is bounded to bootstrap-only behavior.
Per-process PT ownership is explicit and steady-state authoritative.
tasks_for_codex_chirho: Design the exact exec replacement contract and migration plan.

Define what address-space operations must be substrate-only.
Keep the GLOBAL_MAPPER elimination and explicit-PT plan current so short-term session-limit fixes do not reintroduce old address-space debt.
tasks_for_claude_chirho: Implement the replacement/cleanup path incrementally.
Add trace points proving which PT is active at exec, fault, and return-to-user boundaries.
Delete transitional mapping paths after the authoritative path is verified.
Avoid reintroducing singleton-mapper shortcuts in user-memory paths while fixing current SSH lifecycle issues.
tasks_for_gemini_chirho: Research Asterinas and Linux page-table ownership patterns relevant to exec replacement and user-memory authority.
deletion_targets_chirho: user execution routed through transitional boot mappings

workstreams_chirho.why_now_chirho: The current SSH session-limit frontier points directly at fd-table clone/drop semantics and pipe endpoint lifetime, not just inode-mode inference. Temporary exec-time fd-table mirrors must not perturb pipe reader/writer counts.
success_criteria_chirho: Generic dispatch is based on typed file description identity.
Socket/pipe/PTY/regular-file behavior no longer depends on inode-mode guessing in generic syscall paths.
Close and readiness semantics operate on typed endpoint state.
Temporary fd-table clones during fork, exec, or snapshotting do not inflate or suppress pipe endpoint counts.

Plan migration of read, write, poll, select, ioctl, and close semantics to typed OFDs.
Define how to separate fd-table lifetime from OFD lifetime cleanly.
Specify authoritative clone/drop semantics for fd tables and pipe endpoints across fork, exec, CLOEXEC cleanup, and temporary mirror snapshots.
tasks_for_claude_chirho: Implement the typed dispatch layer incrementally.
Migrate syscall paths off is_socket_fd-style inference.
Verify that pipe/socket/PTTY close and readiness semantics still hold under real Dropbear and BusyBox workloads.

workstreams_chirho.title_chirho: Authoritative Teardown, EOF, SIGCHLD, and Session Lifecycle
workstreams_chirho.why_now_chirho: The kernel now sustains 6-7 consecutive SSH sessions and 13 real commands, so the remaining childpipe cleanup and missed-EOF frontier is sharply isolated and worth fixing as generic teardown semantics rather than demo glue.
success_criteria_chirho: 10+ consecutive SSH sessions succeed without QEMU restart and without a kernel-side childpipe cleanup artifact.
Socket EOF, CloseWait, pipe EOF, SIGCHLD, wait4, and session exit ordering are explicit and stable.
Parent select/read observes childpipe write-end closure through endpoint state rather than a workload-specific workaround.
tasks_for_codex_chirho: Own the teardown state-machine design across task, pipe, socket, and session boundaries.
Define publish-before-wake ordering rules.
Break down the current SSH teardown failure into generic endpoint and lifecycle primitives.
Integrate childpipe EOF, SIGCHLD, wait4, and select ordering with the fd-table/OFD lifetime model so the fix lands as one coherent contract.
tasks_for_claude_chirho: Instrument and implement the teardown transitions.
Run SSH multi-connection tests and trace EOF, FIN, SIGCHLD, and select/read behavior.
Delete session-specific patches once the generic teardown model holds.
Keep proving the childpipe close path against repeated SSH sessions and the full 13-command regression set.
tasks_for_gemini_chirho: Audit teardown ordering and endpoint-state model for gaps or hidden race conditions.
deletion_targets_chirho: special-case scheduler nudges kept only for SSH teardown

workstreams_chirho.title_chirho: Unsafe Substrate and Asterinas-Inspired Boundary Discipline
workstreams_chirho.why_now_chirho: Rust is helping, but too many invariants are still social rather than mechanical.
success_criteria_chirho: A smaller set of modules owns trap/syscall frames, page-table mutation, user-memory copy, waitqueue core, and low-level device transport.
Unsafe boundaries are clearer and easier to audit.
Higher-level services consume substrate APIs instead of mutating architecture state directly.
tasks_for_codex_chirho: Define the substrate/service split for Lineluya.

immediate_iteration_chirho.title_chirho: Remove The Childpipe Session-Limit Artifact And Harden Fd/OFD Lifetime
immediate_iteration_chirho.why_chirho: The old BusyBox-applet exec frontier is no longer the day-to-day blocker: Claude has verified 13 SSH commands and 6-7 consecutive sessions. The current kernel-shaped limiter is childpipe cleanup after exec, where temporary fd-table cloning appears to inflate pipe endpoint counts or otherwise prevent authoritative write-end closure observation in the parent select path.
tasks_for_codex_chirho: Define authoritative fd-table clone/drop semantics across fork, exec, CLOEXEC cleanup, and temporary mirror snapshots so pipe endpoint counts cannot drift.

Specify how pipe reader/writer counters relate to Arc lifetime, fd-table entry lifetime, and open-file-description lifetime, and identify what must be deleted if a no-pipe-inc snapshot path becomes permanent.
Decide whether the current childpipe frontier belongs primarily under typed OFD identity or teardown, and produce the deletion plan either way.
Reject PID-specific or workload-specific fixes in generic paths unless they are explicitly temporary diagnostics.
Continuously turn Claude's runtime traces into generic kernel primitives or deletion targets.
tasks_for_claude_chirho: Continue tracing clone_table_chirho, clone_table_no_pipe_inc_chirho, close_chirho, and exec cleanup interactions until the endpoint-lifetime model is explicit.
Implement the chosen authoritative fix and validate it with 10+ consecutive SSH sessions plus the current 13-command regression set.
Keep python3 startup speed and the remaining demo items secondary unless they reveal a missing generic primitive.
Use the PRD decision rule before patching generic paths.
Escalate immediately when the next patch would otherwise be a workaround.
tasks_for_gemini_chirho: Audit proposed fd-table/OFD/pipe lifetime rules or research Linux/Asterinas open-file-description and pipe endpoint lifetime patterns if requested.
definition_of_done_chirho: 10+ consecutive SSH sessions succeed without QEMU restart and without a kernel-side childpipe cleanup cap.
Pipe write-end closure becomes visible to the parent through authoritative endpoint lifetime semantics rather than a workload-specific special case.
The fix does not regress the current 13 verified SSH commands, sqlite3, or python3 workloads.
No new demo glue is introduced to achieve this.
